@@ -161,6 +161,7 @@ The Smstrc*/Ssstrc* extensions impose the following requirements on the implemen
 * When timestamp reporting is enabled (`mstrcctl`.TSEN=1), timestamps follow the requirements described in <<trtime>>.
 * When context reporting is enabled (`mstrcctl`.CEN=1), the context value matches that described in <<trcontext>>.
 * Smstrcev1p0/Ssstrcev1p0 implementations will include trace encapsulation as described in <<trcencap>>, and parameter values as defined in <<trcparam>>.
+* When implicit returns are enabled (`mstrcctl`.EIR=1), the trace encoder must guarantee that only well-behaved returns are implicit; the decoder should never be redirected to the wrong return target.  This preempts use of the call depth counter scheme described in section 3.2.5 of the Efficient Trace for RISC-V Specification v2.0.  The maximum return stack size is 64 entries.
body: I think you should take out the "this pre-empts.." sentence.   Firstly I think it's clear from the previous sentence that return addresses need to be validated.  But more importantly, there are other ways to achieve that.  We have talked about adding a signal to RHTI to allow the hart to pass information to the encoder about whether a return is well predicted.  This allows reuse of the hart's existing return stack and address validation, without duplicating it in the encoder.  That's another extension on the backlog!  But when that is implemented, the encoder doesn't need a call stack but does still need a call counter.  In that case, return_stack_size_p will be 0 and call_counter_size_p will be 6.  The wording must not preclude this use case.

I removed that sentence, and added a note in the parameter section indicating that call_counter_width_p is only listed as 0 because the scheme can result in bad return predictions.  If/when your new extension goes through, you can amend that requirement and allow non-zero values.  See my latest commit.

body: I'm still not happy with that.  The return stack and call counter are not mutually exclusive.  Our implementation uses both: we have a counter associated with every stack entry so that you can keep track of recursive functions without having to burn a stack entry for each one.  So we should still allow non-zero call_counter_size_p even without the new RHTI signal.  The important thing is that the return targets must be compared with the prediction, which you've already stated.
